bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Annual Salary Conversion

If you are a primary school teacher in Victoria or considering a role in the state, understanding how your hourly rate translates to an annual salary is essential. Whether you are negotiating a new job offer or checking your current pay, the formula is straightforward: multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. This article explains the conversion, the role of award rates, casual loading, superannuation, and tax, with a focus on the primary school teacher salary Victoria context.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × Weeks

The standard calculation for annual gross pay is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time employee, the typical week is 38 hours. So if your hourly rate is $30, the annual gross would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. This formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for estimating your total pay.

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, simply double your weekly pay. Using the same $30 per hour example, weekly pay is $30 × 38 = $1,140, so fortnightly gross is $2,280.

### Primary School Teacher Salary Victoria: A Practical Example

Primary school teacher salary Victoria is typically set by the Victorian government's teacher classification and pay scale, or by an enterprise agreement. While we do not have a specific median figure for this occupation, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) provides a useful reference. In May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings in Victoria averaged $2,041.1 per week. This is an average across all industries and occupations, not the median for primary school teachers. It can still give you a sense of the general earnings level in the state.

If you have an hourly rate, you can calculate your own annual salary. For instance, if a primary school teacher earns $45 per hour, the annual gross would be $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920. That figure is before tax and super. Remember, your actual pay may differ if you work part-time or under a different arrangement.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, which equates to $1,004.9 per week for 38 hours. For casual employees, a 25% loading applies, making the casual minimum $33.05 per hour. However, most primary school teachers in Victoria are covered by an award or agreement that sets higher minimum rates. The relevant award is likely the Educational Services (Teachers) Award 2020, which has specific pay scales. Always check the Fair Work Ombudsman's pay guides for the correct classification.

If you are a casual teacher, your base hourly rate should not already include the 25% loading. On our timesheet, you enter your base rate and then check the box to add casual loading on top. This ensures the calculation is accurate.

### Including Superannuation

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For a primary school teacher earning $88,920 per year, the super contribution would be $88,920 × 12% = $10,670.40. This amount is paid by your employer into your super fund and is not deducted from your salary. Your total employment cost to the employer is your gross salary plus super.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay is your gross salary minus tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. Using the $88,920 example, the tax would be approximately $18,967 and the Medicare levy $1,778, leaving a take-home pay of about $68,175. This is an estimate; your actual tax may vary depending on your circumstances, such as HELP repayments or the Medicare levy surcharge. For a more precise calculation, use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool.

### Using Our Timesheet and Pay Guides

Our [timesheet](/) is the home page where you can enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, check the box to add 25% casual loading. The timesheet will then calculate your annual gross, fortnightly pay, weekly pay, and provide estimates for tax and super. For detailed award rates and classifications, refer to our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data). You can also explore [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) information, [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) rules, and [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) details.

Remember, the annual pay shown here is an estimate. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.

For a primary school teacher salary Victoria, understanding these components helps you evaluate job offers, plan your budget, and ensure you are being paid correctly. Use our tools to get a clear picture of your earnings.
